newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50- trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50- trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher on light hog supplies and firm packer demand, livestock dealers said.
At least one major packer Friday said it still needed hogs to fill Monday's slaughter inventory, they said.
Demand could offset reduced competition for live supplies Monday when several hog and pork plants plan to be closed in observance of the Veterans Day holiday.
Hormel Foods Corp Thursday said its Fremont, Neb., hog slaughtering plant and its Austin, Minn., pork processing plant would be closed for the holiday.
Also, Quality Pork Processing Inc's hog slaughtering plant in Austin will be closed Monday. The plant provides fresh pork to Hormel's Austin pork plant.
Total daily slaughter capacity for the plants was about 28,000 head, industry sources said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant Friday could range from $54.00 to $54.50, possibly $55.00.
Illinois top prices for hogs at the plant could range from $53.00 to $53.50 and Indiana/Ohio top plant prices could range from $53.00 to $53.50.
Cash hog prices Monday also could be supported by this week's pork price strength, market sources said.
Increased retail featuring and renewed export business lifted loin prices $4.00 to $6.00 per cwt this week and butts $6.00 to $8.00, according to USDA's national carlot pork trade weekly review.
